Persistent Cache of Downloaded Data

Source: R/cache.R
download_cache.Rd

Lists or clears the data downloaded from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database, STARK-B and ExoMol and kept on disk, so that they are reused in later sessions and without an internet connection.

Usage

download_cache()

clear_download_cache(source = c("nist", "starkb", "exomol"), older_than = NULL)

Arguments

source

The sources to clear: "nist", "starkb" and/or "exomol". Default is all of them.

older_than

Clear only the entries older than this number of days, or NULL (default) for all of them.

Value

download_cache(): a tibble with one row per file of the persistent cache, with its source, file name, size (kB), modified time and age (days); its directory is the attribute dir (NULL when the cache is not enabled). clear_download_cache(): invisibly, the paths of the deleted files. It also clears the session cache of the sources.

Details

Downloaded data are always kept for the R session. To keep them between sessions, set the option specProc.cache, for example in your .Rprofile:

  • options(specProc.cache = TRUE) keeps them in the user cache directory of specProc, given by tools::R_user_dir();

  • options(specProc.cache = "path/to/dir") keeps them in that directory;

  • NULL or FALSE (default) keeps them for the session only.

The results of nist_lines(), nist_ionization_energy(), nist_levels() (and so libs_lines() and line_finder()), starkb_lines() and molecular_spectrum() are then read from the cache when they are there. Entries older than the option specProc.cache_max_age (in days, default 180) are downloaded again, as the databases are updated; when the download fails, the older copy is used with a warning. The NIST and STARK-B entries are small (a few kilobytes to a megabyte); ExoMol line lists can be large, see exomol_datasets().

The cache can also be cleared by deleting its directory.

See also

nist_lines(), starkb_lines(), molecular_spectrum()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

# keep the downloaded data in a directory (here a temporary one)
old <- options(specProc.cache = file.path(tempdir(), "specProc-cache"))
download_cache()
#> # A tibble: 0 × 5
#> # ℹ 5 variables: source <chr>, file <chr>, size <dbl>, modified <dttm>,
#> #   age <dbl>
clear_download_cache()
options(old)
